bull.t: Rapid Revenue Growth And Contracted Backlog
bull.b: Rapid revenue growth and a large contracted backlog indicate strong customer adoption and improving commercial scale. If deployments proceed as planned, the backlog can provide substantial recurring revenue visibility, support operating leverage, and strengthen the company’s position in AI infrastructure.

Project-based financing and sizable customer prepayments reduce the amount of upfront capital the company must fund itself. This structure can improve deployment liquidity, align funding with contracted demand, and support expansion without relying as heavily on equity issuance.

Longer contract durations can improve revenue visibility and make infrastructure investments easier to plan and finance. A customer base spanning multiple AI and enterprise categories, with no customer above 23% of the portfolio, also reduces concentration in any single relationship.

bear.b: Large operating and net losses show that the current revenue base has not yet absorbed the company’s cost structure. Continued losses could consume capital, limit internally funded expansion, and make the expected transition to sustainable profitability dependent on successful execution and rapid scaling.

High leverage reduces financial flexibility while the company is still loss-making and scaling its infrastructure footprint. Debt obligations can constrain capital allocation, increase refinancing and solvency exposure, and make weaker-than-expected deployments more damaging to liquidity and shareholder returns.

bear.t: Cash Flow Quality And Rising Lease Obligations
bear.b: Reported operating cash flow was supported heavily by customer deposits and payables, so it may not represent a sustainable run rate. At the same time, growing GPU lease payments create recurring cash demands, increasing the need for disciplined liquidity management as deployments expand.
